Does the king not know that in our lands there are Christians living under covenants of protection and safe-conduct whose numbers none but Allah can count? Our treatment of them is well known. How, then, can they treat Muslim prisoners in ways that no person of honor or religion would accept? I am not speaking of the king, his household, or his brothers, for Abū al-‘Abbās is deeply grateful to the king and his household and acknowledges the kindness they have shown him. Rather, I am speaking of the populace at large. Are the prisoners not among the king’s subjects? Do not the injunctions of the Messiah and all the other prophets enjoin kindness and good treatment? Where, then, is that?

Moreover, many of them were captured only through treachery, and treachery is forbidden in every religion, revealed law, and system of governance. How, then, can you regard it as lawful to take possession of those captured through treachery? Do you feel safe, despite this, from the Muslims repaying you with some of the same treatment, so that you yourselves become victims of treachery? Allah is their supporter and helper, especially in these times, when the community has mobilized for jihad and prepared for battle. The righteous and the friends of the Most Merciful are eager to obey Him. Commanders of great military prowess have taken charge of the coastal frontier regions. Some of their achievements have already become apparent, and their strength continues to grow.

فُرُشِهَا وَعَلَى أَفْرَاسِهَا:
 مَنْ قَدْ بَلَغَ الْمَلِكُ خَبَرُهُمْ؛ قَدِيمًا وَحَدِيثًا. وَفِيهِمْ الصَّالِحُونَ الَّذِينَ لَا يَرُدُّ اللَّهُ دَعَوَاتِهِمْ وَلَا يُخَيِّبُ طَلَبَاتِهِمْ الَّذِينَ يَغْضَبُ الرَّبُّ لِغَضَبِهِمْ وَيَرْضَى لِرِضَاهُمْ. وَهَؤُلَاءِ التَّتَارُ مَعَ كَثْرَتِهِمْ وَانْتِسَابِهِمْ إلَى الْمُسْلِمِينَ لَمَّا غَضِبَ الْمُسْلِمُونَ عَلَيْهِمْ أَحَاطَ بِهِمْ مِنْ الْبَلَاءِ مَا يَعْظُمُ عَنْ الْوَصْفِ. فَكَيْفَ يَحْسُنُ أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ بِقَوْمِ يُجَاوِرُونَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ مِنْ أَكْثَرِ الْجِهَاتِ أَنْ يُعَامِلُوهُمْ هَذِهِ الْمُعَامَلَةَ الَّتِي لَا يَرْضَاهَا عَاقِلٌ؛ لَا مُسْلِمٌ وَلَا مُعَاهَدٌ. هَذَا وَأَنْتَ تَعْلَمُ أَنَّ الْمُسْلِمِينَ لَا ذَنْبَ لَهُمْ أَصْلًا؛ بَلْ هُمْ الْمَحْمُودُونَ عَلَى مَا فَعَلُوهُ؛ فَإِنَّ الَّذِي أَطْبَقَتْ الْعُقَلَاءُ عَلَى الْإِقْرَارِ بِفَضْلِهِ هُوَ دِينُهُمْ حَتَّى الْفَلَاسِفَةُ أَجْمَعُوا عَلَى أَنَّهُ لَمْ يَطْرُقْ الْعَالَمَ دِينٌ أَفْضَلُ مِنْ هَذَا الدِّينِ. فَقَدْ قَامَتْ الْبَرَاهِينُ عَلَى وُجُوبِ مُتَابَعَتِهِ. ثُمَّ هَذِهِ الْبِلَادُ مَا زَالَتْ بِأَيْدِيهِمْ السَّاحِلُ؛ بَلْ وَقُبْرُصُ أَيْضًا مَا أُخِذَتْ مِنْهُمْ إلَّا مِنْ أَقَلِّ مِنْ ثَلَاثمِائَةِ سَنَةٍ وَقَدْ وَعَدَهُمْ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ أَنَّهُمْ لَا يَزَالُونَ ظَاهِرِينَ إلَى يَوْمِ الْقِيَامَةِ. فَمَا يُؤْمِنُ الْمَلِكُ أَنَّ هَؤُلَاءِ الْأَسْرَى الْمَظْلُومِينَ بِبَلْدَتِهِ يَنْتَقِمُ لَهُمْ رَبُّ الْعِبَادِ وَالْبِلَادِ كَمَا يَنْتَقِمُ لِغَيْرِهِمْ وَمَا يُؤَمِّنُهُ أَنْ تَأْخُذَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ حَمِيَّةُ إسْلَامِهِمْ فَيَنَالُوا مِنْهَا مَا نَالُوا مِنْ غَيْرِهَا وَنَحْنُ إذَا رَأَيْنَا مِنْ الْمَلِكِ وَأَصْحَابِهِ مَا يَصْلُحُ عَامَلْنَاهُمْ بِالْحُسْنَى وَإِلَّا فَمَنْ بُغِيَ عَلَيْهِ لَيَنْصُرَنَّهُ اللَّهُ.
translated_text:
their beds and on horseback—men whose exploits, both past and recent, have reached the king. Among the Muslims are also righteous men whose supplications Allah does not reject and whose requests He does not disappoint; the Lord is angry when they are angry and pleased when they are pleased. These Tatars, despite their great numbers and their affiliation with the Muslims, were beset by calamities beyond description when the Muslims became angry with them.

How, then, O king, can it be fitting for a people who border the Muslims on most sides to treat them in this manner, which no reasonable person would approve, whether a Muslim or someone bound by a covenant? Moreover, you know that the Muslims bear no blame whatsoever; rather, they deserve praise for what they have done. Their religion is the very one whose excellence all reasonable people unanimously acknowledge. Even the philosophers agree that no religion better than this has ever appeared in the world. Conclusive proofs have established the obligation to follow it.

Furthermore, these coastal lands have remained in their hands; indeed, even Cyprus was taken from them less than three hundred years ago. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, promised them that they would remain triumphant until the Day of Resurrection.

What assurance, then, does the king have that the Lord of all people and lands will not avenge these oppressed prisoners in his land, just as He avenges others? And what assurance does he have that the Muslims’ zeal for their faith will not move them to do to his land what they have done to others? If we see proper conduct from the king and his companions, we will treat them kindly. Otherwise, Allah will surely help whoever is wronged.

original_text:
وَأَنْتَ تَعْلَمُ أَنَّ ذَلِكَ مِنْ أَيْسَرِ الْأُمُورِ عَلَى الْمُسْلِمِينَ. وَأَنَا مَا غَرَضِي السَّاعَةَ إلَّا مُخَاطَبَتُكُمْ بِاَلَّتِي هِيَ أَحْسَنُ وَالْمُعَاوَنَةُ عَلَى النَّظَرِ فِي الْعِلْمِ وَاتِّبَاعِ الْحَقِّ وَفِعْلِ مَا يَجِبُ. فَإِنْ كَانَ عِنْدَ الْمَلِكِ مَنْ يَثِقُ بِعَقْلِهِ وَدِينِهِ فَلْيَبْحَثْ مَعَهُ عَنْ أُصُولِ الْعِلْمِ وَحَقَائِقِ الْأَدْيَانِ وَلَا يَرْضَى أَنْ يَكُونَ مِنْ هَؤُلَاءِ النَّصَارَى الْمُقَلِّدِينَ الَّذِينَ لَا يَسْمَعُونَ وَلَا يَعْقِلُونَ؛ إنْ هُمْ إلَّا كَالْأَنْعَامِ؛ بَلْ هُمْ أَضَلُّ سَبِيلًا.
 وَأَصْلُ ذَلِكَ أَنْ تَسْتَعِينَ بِاَللَّهِ وَتَسْأَلَهُ الْهِدَايَةَ وَتَقُولَ:
 اللَّهُمَّ أَرِنِي الْحَقَّ حَقًّا وَأَعِنِّي عَلَى اتِّبَاعِهِ. وَأَرِنِي الْبَاطِلَ بَاطِلًا وَأَعِنِّي عَلَى اجْتِنَابِهِ وَلَا تَجْعَلْهُ مُشْتَبَهًا عَلَيَّ فَأَتَّبِعَ الْهَوَى فَأَضِلَّ.
 وَقُلْ اللَّهُمَّ رَبَّ جِبْرِيلَ وميكائيل وَإِسْرَافِيلَ فَاطِرَ السَّمَوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ عَالِمَ الْغَيْبِ وَالشَّهَادَةِ أَنْتَ تَحْكُمُ بَيْنَ عِبَادِك فِيمَا كَانُوا فِيهِ يَخْتَلِفُونَ:
 اهْدِنِي لِمَا اُخْتُلِفَ فِيهِ مِنْ الْحَقِّ بِإِذْنِك إنَّك تَهْدِي مَنْ تَشَاءُ إلَى صِرَاطٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ. وَالْكِتَابُ لَا يَحْتَمِلُ الْبَسْطَ أَكْثَرَ مِنْ هَذَا؛ لَكِنَّ أَنَا مَا أُرِيدَ لِلْمَلِكِ إلَّا مَا يَنْفَعُهُ فِي الدُّنْيَا وَالْآخِرَةِ وَهُمَا شَيْئَانِ. (أَحَدُهُمَا لَهُ خَاصَّةً وَهُوَ مَعْرِفَتُهُ بِالْعِلْمِ وَالدِّينِ وَانْكِشَافِ الْحَقِّ وَزَوَالِ الشُّبْهَةِ وَعِبَادَةِ اللَّهِ كَمَا أَمَرَ. فَهَذَا خَيْرٌ لَهُ مِنْ مُلْكِ الدُّنْيَا بِحَذَافِيرِهَا. وَهُوَ الَّذِي بَعَثَ بِهِ الْمَسِيحَ وَعَلَّمَهُ الْحَوَارِيِّينَ. (الثَّانِي لَهُ وَلِلْمُسْلِمِينَ وَهُوَ مُسَاعَدَتُهُ لِلْأَسْرَى الَّذِينَ فِي بِلَادِهِ وَإِحْسَانُهُ إلَيْهِمْ وَأَمْرُ رَعِيَّتِهِ بِالْإِحْسَانِ إلَيْهِمْ
translated_text:
And you know that this is among the easiest things for the Muslims to do. My sole purpose now is to address you in the best manner and to help in examining matters of knowledge, following the truth, and doing what is required. If the king has someone whose reason and religious integrity he trusts, let him discuss with that person the foundations of knowledge and the true nature of religions. He should not be content to be among those blindly imitating Christians who neither listen nor reason: they are only like cattle—indeed, they are even further astray.

The foundation of this is to seek Allah’s help, ask Him for guidance, and say:

“O Allah, show me the truth as truth and help me to follow it. Show me falsehood as falsehood and help me to avoid it. Do not let it become unclear to me, lest I follow my desires and go astray.”

And say:

“O Allah, Lord of Gabriel, Michael, and Isrāfīl, Originator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the seen, You judge between Your servants concerning that over which they differed. By Your permission, guide me to the truth concerning which there is disagreement. Indeed, You guide whom You will to a straight path.”

This letter does not allow for a fuller discussion than this. I desire for the king only what will benefit him in this world and the Hereafter, and that consists of two things.

(The first) concerns him alone: that he gain understanding of knowledge and religion, that the truth become clear to him and doubt be dispelled, and that he worship Allah as He has commanded. This is better for him than dominion over the entire world. It is what the Messiah was sent with and taught the disciples.

(The second) concerns both him and the Muslims: that he assist the prisoners in his land, treat them kindly, and command his subjects to treat them kindly

original_text:
وَالْمُعَاوَنَةُ لَنَا عَلَى خَلَاصِهِمْ؛ فَإِنَّ فِي الْإِسَاءَةِ إلَيْهِمْ دَرْكًا عَلَى الْمَلِكِ فِي دِينِهِ وَدِينِ اللَّهِ تَعَالَى وَدَرْكًا مِنْ جِهَةِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ وَفِي الْمُعَاوَنَةِ عَلَى خَلَاصِهِمْ حَسَنَةٌ لَهُ فِي دِينِهِ وَدِينِ اللَّهِ تَعَالَى وَعِنْدَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ؛ وَكَانَ الْمَسِيحُ أَعْظَمَ النَّاسِ تَوْصِيَةً بِذَلِكَ.
 وَمِنْ الْعَجَبِ كُلَّ الْعَجَبِ أَنْ يَأْسِرَ النَّصَارَى قَوْمًا غَدْرًا أَوْ غَيْرَ غَدْرٍ وَلَمْ يُقَاتِلُوهُمْ وَالْمَسِيحُ يَقُولُ:
 
" مَنْ لَطَمَك عَلَى خَدِّك الْأَيْمَنِ فَأَدِرْ لَهُ خَدَّك الْأَيْسَرَ وَمَنْ أَخَذَ رِدَاءَك فَأَعْطِهِ قَمِيصَك "
 وَكُلَّمَا كَثُرَتْ الْأَسْرَى عِنْدَكُمْ كَانَ أَعْظَمَ لِغَضَبِ اللَّهِ وَغَضَبِ عِبَادِهِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ؛ فَكَيْفَ يُمْكِنُ السُّكُوتُ عَلَى أَسْرَى الْمُسْلِمِينَ فِي قُبْرُصَ سِيَّمَا وَعَامَّةُ هَؤُلَاءِ الْأَسْرَى قَوْمٌ فُقَرَاءُ وَضُعَفَاءُ لَيْسَ لَهُمْ مَنْ يَسْعَى فِيهِمْ. وَهَذَا أَبُو الْعَبَّاسِ مَعَ أَنَّهُ مِنْ عِبَادِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ وَلَهُ عِبَادَةٌ وَفَقْرٌ وَفِيهِ مَشْيَخَةٌ وَمَعَ هَذَا فَمَا كَادَ يَحْصُلُ لَهُ فِدَاؤُهُ إلَّا بِالشِّدَّةِ. وَدِينُ الْإِسْلَامِ يَأْمُرُنَا أَنْ نُعِينَ الْفَقِيرَ وَالضَّعِيفَ. فَالْمَلِكُ أَحَقُّ أَنْ يُسَاعِدَ عَلَى ذَلِكَ مِنْ وُجُوهٍ كَثِيرَةٍ؛ لَا سِيَّمَا وَالْمَسِيحُ يُوصِي بِذَلِكَ فِي الْإِنْجِيلِ وَيَأْمُرُ بِالرَّحْمَةِ الْعَامَّةِ وَالْخَيْرِ الشَّامِلِ كَالشَّمْسِ وَالْمَطَرِ. وَالْمَلِكُ وَأَصْحَابُهُ إذَا عَاوَنُونَا عَلَى تَخْلِيصِ الْأَسْرَى وَالْإِحْسَانِ إلَيْهِمْ كَانَ الْحَظُّ الْأَوْفَرُ لَهُمْ فِي ذَلِكَ فِي الدُّنْيَا وَالْآخِرَةِ. أَمَّا فِي الْآخِرَةِ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ يُثِيبُ عَلَى ذَلِكَ وَيَأْجُرُ عَلَيْهِ وَهَذَا مِمَّا لَا رَيْبَ فِيهِ عِنْدَ الْعُلَمَاءِ الْمَسِيحِيِّينَ
translated_text:
and help us secure their release. For mistreating them makes the king answerable under his own religion and the religion of Allah Most High, and answerable to the Muslims. Helping to secure their release, however, is a good deed to his credit in his own religion, in the religion of Allah Most High, and in the eyes of the Muslims. The Messiah was foremost among those who urged such conduct.

It is utterly astonishing that Christians should take people captive—whether treacherously or otherwise—when those people have not fought them, while the Messiah says:

“Whoever slaps you on your right cheek, turn your left cheek to him; and whoever takes your cloak, give him your shirt.”

The more captives you hold, the greater the anger of Allah and His Muslim servants. How, then, can we remain silent about the Muslim captives in Cyprus, especially when most of these captives are poor and weak, with no one to work for their release? Take Abū al-ʿAbbās: although he is among the devout Muslims, a man of worship and poverty with standing as a shaykh, even his ransom was secured only with great difficulty.

The religion of Islam commands us to help the poor and the weak. For many reasons, the king has an even greater obligation to help in this, especially since the Messiah urges it in the Gospel and commands mercy for all and goodness that extends to everyone, like sunshine and rain. If the king and his companions help us free the captives and treat them kindly, they will gain the greatest share of benefit from this in this world and the Hereafter. As for the Hereafter, Allah will reward and recompense them for it. This is something about which there is no doubt among Christian scholars

original_text:
الَّذِينَ لَا يَتَّبِعُونَ الْهَوَى؛ بَلْ كُلُّ مَنْ اتَّقَى اللَّهَ وَأَنْصَفَ عَلِمَ أَنَّهُمْ أُسِرُوا بِغَيْرِ حَقٍّ لَا سِيَّمَا مَنْ أُخِذَ غَدْرًا وَاَللَّهُ تَعَالَى لَمْ يَأْمُرْ الْمَسِيحَ وَلَا أَحَدًا مِنْ الْحَوَارِيِّينَ وَلَا مَنْ اتَّبَعَ الْمَسِيحَ عَلَى دِينِهِ؛ لَا بِأَسْرِ أَهْلِ مِلَّةِ إبْرَاهِيمَ وَلَا بِقَتْلِهِمْ. وَكَيْفَ وَعَامَّةُ النَّصَارَى يُقِرُّونَ بِأَنَّ مُحَمَّدًا رَسُولُ الْأُمِّيِّينَ فَكَيْفَ يَجُوزُ أَنْ يُقَاتِلَ أَهْلَ دِينٍ اتَّبَعُوا رَسُولَهُمْ.
 فَإِنْ قَالَ قَائِلٌ:
 هُمْ قَاتَلُونَا أَوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ.
 قِيلَ:
 هَذَا بَاطِلٌ فِيمَنْ غَدَرْتُمْ بِهِ وَمَنْ بَدَأْتُمُوهُ بِالْقِتَالِ. وَأَمَّا مَنْ بَدَأَكُمْ مِنْهُمْ فَهُوَ مَعْذُورٌ لِأَنَّ اللَّهَ تَعَالَى أَمَرَهُ بِذَلِكَ وَرَسُولُهُ بَلْ الْمَسِيحُ وَالْحَوَارِيُّونَ أَخَذَ عَلَيْهِمْ الْمَوَاثِيقَ بِذَلِكَ وَلَا يَسْتَوِي مَنْ عَمِلَ بِطَاعَةِ اللَّهِ وَرُسُلِهِ وَدَعَا إلَى عِبَادَتِهِ وَدِينِهِ وَأَقَرَّ بِجَمِيعِ الْكُتُبِ وَالرُّسُلِ وَقَاتَلَ لِتَكُونَ كَلِمَةُ اللَّهِ هِيَ الْعُلْيَا وَلِيَكُونَ الدِّينُ كُلُّهُ لِلَّهِ وَمَنْ قَاتَلَ فِي هَوَى نَفْسِهِ وَطَاعَةِ شَيْطَانِهِ عَلَى خِلَافِ أَمْرِ اللَّهِ وَرُسُلِهِ. وَمَا زَالَ فِي النَّصَارَى مِنْ الْمُلُوكِ وَالْقِسِّيسِينَ وَالرُّهْبَانِ وَالْعَامَّةِ مَنْ لَهُ مَزِيَّةٌ عَلَى غَيْرِهِ فِي الْمَعْرِفَةِ وَالدِّينِ؛ فَيَعْرِفُ بَعْضَ الْحَقِّ وَيَنْقَادُ لِكَثِيرِ مِنْهُ وَيَعْرِفُ مِنْ قَدْرِ الْإِسْلَامِ وَأَهْلِهِ مَا يَجْهَلُهُ غَيْرُهُ فَيُعَامِلُهُمْ مُعَامَلَةً تَكُونُ نَافِعَةً لَهُ فِي الدُّنْيَا وَالْآخِرَةِ. ثُمَّ فِي فِكَاكِ الْأَسِيرِ وَثَوَابِ الْعِتْقِ مِنْ كَلَامِ الْأَنْبِيَاءِ وَالصِّدِّيقِينَ مَا هُوَ مَعْرُوفٌ لِمَنْ طَلَبَهُ فَمَهْمَا عَمِلَ الْمَلِكُ مَعَهُمْ وَجَدَ ثَمَرَتَهُ.

Allah Most High did not command the Messiah, any of the disciples, or anyone who followed the Messiah’s religion to capture or kill those who follow the religion of Abraham. How could that be, when most Christians acknowledge that Muhammad is the messenger to the unlettered? How, then, can it be permissible to fight people who have followed their messenger?

If someone says, “They fought us first,” the answer is:

This is false in the case of those whom you betrayed and those against whom you initiated hostilities. As for those among them who fought you first, they are excused, for Allah Most High and His Messenger commanded them to do so. Indeed, even the Messiah and the disciples were bound by covenants to that effect. Those who obey Allah and His messengers, call others to His worship and His religion, acknowledge all the Scriptures and messengers, and fight so that Allah’s word may be supreme and all worship may be devoted to Allah alone are not equal to those who fight to satisfy their own desires and obey their devil, contrary to the command of Allah and His messengers.

Among Christian kings, priests, monks, and ordinary people, there have always been those who surpass others in knowledge and religious devotion. Such a person recognizes some of the truth and submits to much of it, and understands the worth of Islam and its followers in ways that others do not. He therefore treats them in a manner that benefits him in this world and the Hereafter.

Furthermore, the sayings of the prophets and the steadfastly truthful concerning the release of captives and the reward for freeing slaves are well known to anyone who seeks them out. Whatever the king does in his dealings with them, he will reap its fruits.

As for this world, the Muslims are more capable than anyone else of repaying both kindness and harm. Woe—utter woe—to anyone against whom they wage war! The king must surely have heard the historical accounts and learned that small groups of Muslims have repeatedly defeated Christians and others many times their number. What, then, when the Muslims themselves outnumber them? He will also have heard of the famous battles of earlier and more recent times, such as forty thousand defeating more than four hundred thousand Christians, most of them horsemen.

The Muslims guarding the frontiers have continued to enter Christian lands despite their small numbers and the Muslim kings’ preoccupation with other matters. How much more so now that Allah Most High has blessed the Muslims with unity, numerous armies, valiant commanders, lofty resolve, and a desire for whatever brings them nearer to Allah Most High; when they believe that jihad is the best of voluntary deeds and affirm the promise their Prophet made them when he said:

“The martyr is granted six blessings: he is forgiven with the first drop of his blood; he sees his place in Paradise; he is clothed in the robe of faith; he is married to seventy-two of the maidens of Paradise with beautiful, wide eyes; he is protected from the trial of the grave; and he is kept safe from the greatest terror on the Day of Resurrection.”

Furthermore, there are many times as many Christians in their lands as there are Muslims among you. Among them are Christian leaders with few equals across the sea. As for the Muslim captives, none of them is someone the Muslims need or from whom they derive benefit. We seek their release only for the sake of Allah Most High, out of compassion for them and to draw nearer to Him on the Day when He rewards

Abū al-‘Abbās, the bearer of this letter, has spoken among us of the virtues of the king and his brothers, inclining our hearts towards him. I have therefore written to the king upon learning of his desire for goodness and his inclination towards knowledge and religion. In offering sincere counsel to the king and his companions and seeking their welfare, I am among the representatives of the Messiah and all the other prophets. For Muhammad’s community is the best community brought forth for mankind: they desire good for all people in this world and the Hereafter, enjoin what is right, forbid what is wrong, call them to Allah, and help them pursue what benefits their religious and worldly affairs.

If the king has received reports disparaging some of them or their religion, then either the informant was lying or he failed to understand the reports’ meaning and the actual circumstances. If, however, he truthfully reported sins, indecencies, or injustices committed by some of them, such things inevitably occur in every community. Indeed, the evil found among Muslims is far less than that found among others, while the good found among them has no equal elsewhere.

The king, and every sensible person, knows that most Christians depart from the precepts of the Messiah and the Apostles and from the epistles of Paul and other saints—even if most of what they retain of Christianity consists of drinking wine, eating pork, venerating the cross, and invented ordinances for which Allah has sent down no authority—and that some of them regard as lawful certain things forbidden by Christian religious law. This concerns what they themselves acknowledge. As for

their failure to abide by what they do not acknowledge, that applies to them all. Indeed, we have an established report from the Messenger of Allah—the truthful one whose truthfulness is confirmed, may Allah bless him and grant him peace:

“The Messiah, Jesus son of Mary, will descend here among us at the white minaret in Damascus, resting his hands on the shoulders of two angels. He will break the cross, kill swine, abolish the jizya, and accept nothing from anyone but Islam. He will kill the messiah of misguidance, the one-eyed Dajjāl, whom the Jews will follow. The Muslims will gain power over the Jews, until trees and stones say: ‘O Muslim, there is a Jew behind me; kill him.’ Allah will exact retribution from the Jews on behalf of the Messiah son of Mary, the messiah of guidance, for harming him and rejecting him when he was sent to them.”

As for what has been related to us concerning the Christians, and what Allah will do to them by granting the Muslims victory and power over them, this is something I will not tell the king, lest it distress him. My sincere counsel to him, however, is that whoever has previously shown kindness to the Muslims and been favourably disposed towards them will fare well with them, in proportion to the good he has done. For Allah says:

“So whoever does an atom’s weight of good will see it.”

“And whoever does an atom’s weight of evil will see it.”

I conclude this letter by urging that Shaykh Abū al-ʿAbbās and the other captives be treated well and assisted, that the followers of the Quran in their custody be treated gently, and that no attempt be made to change the religion of any one of them. The king will see the outcome of all this. We shall repay the king for it many times beyond what he has in mind. We ask Allah to help the king pursue what is truly in his best interest in Allah’s sight, to choose for him the words that are best for him in Allah’s sight, and to grant him a good end. Praise be to Allah, Lord of all worlds. May His blessings be upon His messengers, especially Muhammad, the last of the prophets and messengers, and may peace be upon them all.

He was asked:

Is Medina part of al-Shām (Greater Syria)?

He answered:

The Prophet’s city—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—is part of the Hijaz, by the agreement of the scholars. No one, Muslim or otherwise, has said that the Prophet’s city is part of al-Shām. Only someone ignorant of the boundaries of al-Shām and the Hijaz, and ignorant of what the jurists, linguists and others have said, would make such a claim.

However, people do say, “Medina is Syrian and Mecca is Yemeni,” meaning that Medina is closer to al-Shām and Mecca is closer to Yemen. Mecca is not part of Yemen, nor is Medina part of al-Shām.

During his final illness, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, commanded that the Jews and Christians leave the Arabian Peninsula—which is the Hijaz—so they were expelled by ʿUmar

and with those who follow them in righteousness until the Day of Judgment.

He replied:

Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds. As for their claim that the Muslims wronged them by closing these churches, this is a lie that contradicts the consensus of the Muslims. The Muslim scholars of the four schools—those of Abū Hanīfa, Mālik, al-Shāfiʿī, and Ahmad—and other imams, such as Sufyān al-Thawrī, al-Awzāʿī, al-Layth ibn Saʿd, and others, together with their predecessors among the Companions and Successors—may Allah be pleased with them all—agree that if the ruler demolished every church in territory conquered by force, such as Egypt, the Sawād region of Iraq, the Syrian mainland, and similar territories, exercising his legal judgment and following those who hold this view, he would not thereby be acting unjustly. Rather, those who hold this view are obliged to obey him and assist him in doing so. If they refused to submit to the Muslims’ ruling concerning them, they would be breaking the covenant, and their lives and property would thereby become forfeit.

As for their assertion that these churches have stood since the time of the Commander of the Faithful, ʿUmar ibn al-Khattāb—may Allah be pleased with him—and that the Rightly Guided Caliphs allowed them to retain them, this too is a lie. For it is known through mass transmission that Cairo was built more than three hundred years after ʿUmar ibn al-Khattāb—may Allah be pleased with him. It was built after Baghdad, Basra, Kufa, and Wāsit. The Muslims have unanimously agreed that, in cities founded by Muslims, it was not

How much more, then, does this apply to Muslim cities! Indeed, if they had a church in territory conquered by force, such as Iraq, Egypt, and similar lands, and the Muslims built a city around it, the Muslims would be entitled to take possession of that church, so that no church would remain in Muslim cities without a covenant protecting it.

For in Sunan Abī Dāwūd, Ibn ʿAbbās—may Allah be pleased with them both—reports through a good chain of transmission that the Prophet—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—said:

“Two directions of prayer may not coexist in one land, and no jizya is due from a Muslim.”

In a city or village inhabited by Muslims and containing their mosques, nothing among the outward symbols of unbelief may be displayed—neither churches nor anything else—unless those concerned have a covenant, in which case their covenant must be honoured. Thus, even if a church had existed on the site of Cairo or a similar city before its construction, the Muslims would have been entitled to take possession of it, since the territory was conquered by force. How much more so when these churches were newly established by the Christians! For nearly two hundred years, Cairo’s rulers did not follow the law of Islam.

They outwardly professed to be Rāfidīs, while inwardly they were Ismāʿīlīs, Nusayrīs, and Qarmatian esotericists. As al-Ghazālī—may Allah Most High have mercy on him—said of them in the book he wrote to refute them:

“The outward aspect of their doctrine is Rāfidism; its inward reality is pure unbelief.”

Indeed, they explicitly declared that their claimed lineage was false and that their ancestor was ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Maymūn al-Qaddāh, who was not a member of the household of the Messenger of Allah—may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

Scholars wrote works on this subject. Those who testified to this included Shaykh Abū al-Hasan al-Qudūrī, the Hanafī imam; Shaykh Abū Hāmid al-Isfarāyīnī, the Shāfiʿī imam; Judge Abū Yaʿlā, the Hanbalī imam; and Abū Muhammad ibn Abī Zayd, the Mālikī imam. Judge Abū Bakr ibn al-Tayyib wrote a book exposing their secrets, entitled “Uncovering Secrets and Tearing Away Veils,” concerning the doctrine of the esoteric Qarmatians.

The Ismāʿīlīs, Nusayrīs, Druze, and others like them found in Muslim lands are among their followers. They were the ones who helped the Tatars fight the Muslims, and Hulagu’s minister, al-Nasīr al-Tūsī, was one of their leading authorities. These people harbour the greatest enmity towards the Muslims and their rulers, followed by the Rāfidīs. The Rāfidīs ally themselves with those who fight the people of the Sunnah and the community; they ally themselves with the Tatars and with the Christians.

On the coast, there was a truce between the Rāfidīs and the Franks, to the point that the Rāfidīs transported the Muslims’ horses and weapons to Cyprus, along with the sultan’s young retainers, other soldiers, and boys. Baghdad’s vizier, Ibn al-Alqamī the Rāfidī, was the one who conspired against the Muslims and corresponded with the Tatars until, through cunning and deception, he brought them into Iraq and forbade the people to fight them.

Those knowledgeable about Islam have recognized that the Rāfidīs side with the enemies of the religion.

When they ruled Cairo, their vizier was at one time a Jew and at another an Armenian Christian. The Christians gained strength through that Armenian Christian and built many churches in Egypt under the rule of those hypocritical Rāfidīs. They used to proclaim in Bayn al-Qasrayn:

“Whoever curses and reviles shall receive a dinar and an irdabb of grain.”

During their rule, the Christians seized the Syrian coast from the Muslims, until Nūr al-Dīn and Salāh al-Dīn reconquered it. During their rule, the Franks reached Bilbays, and they were defeated by the Franks, for they were hypocrites. The Christians helped them, but Allah does not grant victory to hypocrites who ally themselves with the Christians. They therefore sent to Nūr al-Dīn seeking help, and he sent them reinforcements under Asad al-Dīn and his nephew Salāh al-Dīn.

When the warriors fighting in Allah’s cause arrived in Egypt, the Rāfidīs sided with the Christians and sought to fight those Muslim warriors. A series of events known to the people ensued, until Salāh al-Dīn killed their leader, Shāwar. and Muslim’s, and similar works. The teachings of the imams are expounded there, and Allah’s pleasure is invoked upon the Rightly Guided Caliphs. Before that, however, they had been among the worst of people. Among them were people who worshipped the stars and observed their movements, and Dahrī heretics who believed in neither the Hereafter, Paradise, nor Hell, and did not consider prayer, zakat, fasting, or pilgrimage obligatory. The best among them were the Rāfidīs, yet the Rāfidīs are the worst of the groups that profess allegiance to the qiblah.

For this and similar reasons, new churches were built in Cairo and elsewhere. There had already been old churches in the Egyptian countryside, but the Muslims allowed them to retain those churches when they conquered the land, because the farmers were all Christians, not Muslims; only the troops were Muslims. They allowed them to remain, just as the Prophet—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—allowed the Jews to remain at Khaybar after conquering it, because the Jews were farmers while the Muslims were occupied with jihad.

Later, during the caliphate of Umar ibn al-Khattāb—may Allah be pleased with him—when the Muslims had grown in number and no longer needed the Jews, the Commander of the Faithful expelled them from Khaybar, as the Prophet—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—had commanded when he said:

“Expel the Jews and Christians from the Arabian Peninsula.”

Thus, not a single Jew remained in Khaybar.

The same applies to a village whose inhabitants are Christians, with no Muslims or Muslim mosque among them: if the Muslims allow them to retain their existing churches, that is permissible, as the Muslims have done. But if Muslims settle there

and build their mosques there, then the Prophet—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—has said:

“It is not right for there to be two qiblahs in one land.”

Another report states:

“A house of mercy and a house of punishment cannot coexist.”

The Muslims have become numerous in Egypt, and the land has grown so populous in these times that its inhabitants now number several times as many as in the days of Salāh al-Dīn. Salāh al-Dīn and his family did not take the Christians as allies, nor did they employ any of them in any aspect of Muslim affairs whatsoever. For this reason, they were supported and granted victory over their enemies despite their limited wealth and numbers.

The Christians and Tatars only grew powerful after the death of al-‘Ādil, Salāh al-Dīn’s brother. Some kings even gave them Muslim cities, and troubles arose because of neglecting what Allah and His Messenger—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—had commanded. For Allah Most High says:

“Allah will surely support those who support Him. Indeed, Allah is Powerful and Almighty.”

Allah Most High also says:

“Those who, if We establish them in the land, establish prayer, give zakat, enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong. And to Allah belongs the outcome of all matters.”

Thus, rulers who demolished their churches and enforced Allah’s commands concerning them, such as Umar ibn Abd al-Azīz, Hārūn al-Rashīd, and others like them, were supported and granted victory. Those who acted otherwise were defeated and subjugated. Strife among the Muslims multiplied, and they became divided in their allegiance to their kings, only from the time of the involvement of

the Christians with the rulers in Egypt, during the reign of al-Mu‘izz, the vizierate of al-Fā’iz, the dispersal of the Bahriyya, and other such events.

Allah Most High says in His Book:

“Our word has already been given to Our servants, the messengers: they will surely be helped, and Our forces will certainly prevail.”

He Most High also says in His Book:

“We will surely support Our messengers and those who believe, both in the life of this world and on the Day when the witnesses stand forth.”

He Most High says:

“O you who believe, if you support Allah, He will support you and make your feet firm.”

It is authentically reported that the Prophet—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—said:

“A group of my ummah will continue to prevail upon the truth, unharmed by those who abandon them or oppose them, until the Hour comes.”

Anyone familiar with the history of peoples and their kings will see that those who most strongly supported the religion of Islam, strove hardest against its enemies, and most faithfully obeyed Allah and His Messenger enjoyed the greatest support, obedience, and respect. This has been so from the time of the Commander of the Faithful, Umar ibn al-Khattāb—may Allah be pleased with him—until the present.

During the caliphate of Umar ibn Abd al-Azīz and other caliphs, the Muslims took many churches from them in lands conquered by force, after they had been allowed to retain them. No Muslim objected to this. It is therefore clear that demolishing churches in lands conquered by force is permissible, provided that doing so causes no harm to the Muslims. Those who refrained from taking action against them did so because the Muslims were few in number, or for similar reasons, just as the Prophet—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—refrained from expelling the Jews until they were expelled by Umar ibn al-Khattāb

translated_text:
can only be achieved by upholding Allah’s religion, making His word prevail, and humbling the enemies of Allah Most High. Let anyone seeking a lesson consider the conduct of Nūr al-Dīn, Saladin, and then al-ʿĀdil: how Allah established their power, supported them, enabled them to conquer lands, and humbled their enemies before them because of what they did in this regard. Let him also consider the conduct of those who allied themselves with the Christians, and how Allah Most High humbled and frustrated them. The Muslims have no need of them, and all praise belongs to Allah.

Khālid ibn al-Walīd—may Allah be pleased with him—wrote to ʿUmar ibn al-Khattāb—may Allah be pleased with him—saying:

“There is a Christian scribe in Syria without whom its land-tax administration cannot function.”

He wrote back: “Do not employ him.”

Khālid wrote: “We cannot do without him.”

ʿUmar wrote back: “Do not employ him.”

Khālid wrote: “If we do not appoint him, the revenue will be lost.”

ʿUmar—may Allah be pleased with him—wrote back: “The Christian is dead. Peace.”

It is established in the authentic collection that a polytheist caught up with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, intending to fight alongside him. The Prophet told him: “I do not seek the assistance of a polytheist.”

Just as employing troops to fight in Allah’s cause is only proper when they are Muslims and believers, so too can those who assist the troops with their finances and duties set their affairs right only if they are Muslims and believers. Among the Muslims are enough people to meet all their needs, and all praise belongs to Allah.

Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī—may Allah be pleased with him—went in to see ʿUmar ibn al-Khattāb—may Allah be pleased with him—

" لِأَنَّهُ نَصْرَانِيٌّ "

 لَا تُعِزُّوهُمْ بَعْدَ أَنْ أَذَلَّهُمْ اللَّهُ وَلَا تَأْمَنُوهُمْ بَعْدَ أَنْ خَوَّنَهُمْ اللَّهُ وَلَا تُصَدِّقُوهُمْ بَعْدَ أَنْ أَكْذَبَهُمْ اللَّهُ. وَالْمُسْلِمُونَ فِي مَشَارِقِ الْأَرْضِ وَمَغَارِبِهَا قُلُوبُهُمْ وَاحِدَةٌ مُوَالِيَةٌ لِلَّهِ وَلِرَسُولِهِ وَلِعِبَادِهِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ مُعَادِيَةٌ لِأَعْدَاءِ اللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ وَأَعْدَاءِ عِبَادِهِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَقُلُوبُهُمْ الصَّادِقَةُ وَأَدْعِيَتُهُمْ الصَّالِحَةُ هِيَ الْعَسْكَرُ الَّذِي لَا يُغْلَبُ وَالْجُنْدُ الَّذِي لَا يُخْذَلُ فَإِنَّهُمْ هُمْ الطَّائِفَةُ الْمَنْصُورَةُ إلَى يَوْمِ الْقِيَامَةِ كَمَا أَخْبَرَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ.

{إنْ تَمْسَسْكُمْ حَسَنَةٌ تَسُؤْهُمْ وَإِنْ تُصِبْكُمْ سَيِّئَةٌ يَفْرَحُوا بِهَا وَإِنْ تَصْبِرُوا وَتَتَّقُوا لَا يَضُرُّكُمْ كَيْدُهُمْ شَيْئًا إنَّ اللَّهَ بِمَا يَعْمَلُونَ مُحِيطٌ}
 وَقَالَ تَعَالَى: {يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لَا تَتَّخِذُوا الْيَهُودَ
translated_text:
—may Allah be pleased with him—and presented him with the accounts of Iraq. Impressed by them, he said:

“Call your scribe to read them to me.”

He replied, “He does not enter the mosque.”

“Why not?” he asked.

“Because he is a Christian,” he replied.

Then Umar—may Allah be pleased with him—struck at him with his whip; had it hit him, it would have hurt him. He then said:

“Do not honour them after Allah has humbled them. Do not trust them after Allah has declared them untrustworthy. Do not believe them after Allah has declared them liars.”

The Muslims throughout the East and West are united in heart, loyal to Allah, His Messenger, and His believing servants, and hostile to the enemies of Allah and His Messenger and the enemies of His believing servants. Their sincere hearts and righteous supplications are the army that cannot be defeated and the host that will never be forsaken. For they are the victorious group until the Day of Resurrection, as the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, foretold.

Allah Most High said:

“O you who believe, do not take as confidants those outside your ranks. They spare no effort to corrupt your affairs and wish to see you suffer. Hatred has already appeared from their mouths, but what their hearts conceal is greater. We have made the signs clear to you, if you will use your reason.”

“Here you are, loving them while they do not love you, although you believe in all the Scripture. When they meet you, they say, ‘We believe.’ But when they are alone, they bite their fingertips in rage at you. Say, ‘Die in your rage!’ Indeed, Allah knows what lies within the hearts.”

“If something good happens to you, it distresses them; but if misfortune befalls you, they rejoice in it. Yet if you remain patient and mindful of Allah, their plotting will not harm you at all. Indeed, Allah encompasses all that they do.”

And He Most High said: “O you who believe, do not take the Jews

and the Christians as allies. They are allies of one another. Whoever among you takes them as allies is one of them. Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.”

“Then you see those in whose hearts is a disease rushing to their side, saying, ‘We fear that misfortune may befall us.’ But perhaps Allah will bring victory or a decision from Him, and then they will regret what they concealed within themselves.”

“The believers will say, ‘Are these the ones who swore their most solemn oaths by Allah that they were with you?’ Their deeds have come to nothing, and they have become losers.”

“O you who believe, whoever among you turns back from his religion—Allah will bring forth a people whom He loves and who love Him, humble towards the believers and stern towards the disbelievers, striving in the cause of Allah and fearing no blame from anyone. That is Allah’s bounty, which He grants to whom He wills. Allah is boundless in bounty, All-Knowing.”

“Your only allies are Allah, His Messenger, and the believers who establish prayer, give zakah, and bow down in worship.”

“Whoever takes Allah, His Messenger, and the believers as allies—indeed, the party of Allah will be victorious.”

These noble verses contain a lesson for people of understanding. Allah Most High revealed them because, in Medina, the Prophet’s city, there were non-Muslims under Muslim protection who possessed power and strength during the lifetime of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. There were also groups of Muslims whose certainty and faith were weak, and among them were hypocrites who outwardly professed Islam while inwardly harbouring disbelief, such as Abdullah ibn Ubayy, the leader of the hypocrites, and others like him. They feared that the disbelievers might gain the upper hand, so they allied themselves with them and took them into their confidence.

Allah Most High said:

“Then you see those in whose hearts is a disease”—that is, hypocrisy and weakness of faith—“rushing to their side”

—that is, in assisting them—“saying, ‘We fear that misfortune may befall us.’” Allah Most High then said:

“But perhaps Allah will bring victory or a decision from Him, and then they will”—meaning these hypocrites who ally themselves with non-Muslims under Muslim protection—“regret what they concealed within themselves.”

“The believers will say, ‘Are these the ones who swore their most solemn oaths by Allah that they were with you?’ Their deeds have come to nothing, and they have become losers.”

Those with experience know that Jews, Christians, and hypocrites living under Muslim protection correspond with their coreligionists, conveying news of the Muslims and whatever secrets of theirs they discover. Such reports from those under Muslim protection to their coreligionists have led to Muslims being seized in the lands of the Tatars, people being taken captive, and other consequences.

Among the well-known verses of poetry are these words:

Every enmity may yet turn to affection,
Except the enmity of one who opposes you in religion.

For this and other reasons, they were prohibited from holding authority over Muslims or managing the interests of Muslims who strengthen them or surpass them in experience and trustworthiness. Indeed, employing someone less capable than they are is more beneficial to Muslims in their religious and worldly affairs. A little lawful provision is blessed, whereas abundant unlawful wealth vanishes and Allah Most High wipes it out.

Allah knows best. May Allah bless Muhammad, his family, and his Companions, and grant them peace.

عَنْ نَصْرَانِيٍّ قِسِّيسٍ بِجَانِبِ دَارِهِ سَاحَةٌ بِهَا كَنِيسَةٌ خَرَابٌ لَا سَقْفَ لَهَا وَلَمْ يَعْلَمْ أَحَدٌ مِنْ الْمُسْلِمِينَ وَقْتَ خَرَابِهَا. فَاشْتَرَى الْقِسِّيسُ السَّاحَةَ وَعَمَّرَهَا وَأَدْخَلَ الْكَنِيسَةَ فِي الْعِمَارَةِ وَأَصْلَحَ حِيطَانَهَا وَعَمَّرَهَا وَبَقِيَ يَجْمَعُ النَّصَارَى فِيهَا وَأَظْهَرُوا شِعَارَهُمْ وَطَلَبَهُ بَعْضُ الْحُكَّامِ فَتَقَوَّى وَاعْتَضَدَ بِبَعْضِ الْأَعْرَابِ وَأَظْهَرَ الشَّرَّ.
فَأَجَابَ:
لَيْسَ لَهُ أَنْ يُحْدِثَ مَا ذَكَرَهُ مِنْ الْكَنِيسَةِ وَإِنْ كَانَ هُنَاكَ آثَارُ كَنِيسَةٍ قَدِيمَةٍ بِبَرِّ الشَّامِ فَإِنَّ بَرَّ الشَّامِ فَتَحَهُ الْمُسْلِمُونَ عَنْوَةً وَمَلَكُوا تِلْكَ الْكَنَائِسَ؛ وَجَازَ لَهُمْ تَخْرِيبُهَا بِاتِّفَاقِ الْعُلَمَاءِ وَإِنَّمَا تَنَازَعُوا فِي وُجُوبِ تَخْرِيبِهَا. وَلَيْسَ لِأَحَدِ أَنْ يُعَاوِنَهُ عَلَى إحْدَاثِ ذَلِكَ وَيَجِبُ عُقُوبَةُ مَنْ أَعَانَهُ عَلَى ذَلِكَ. وَأَمَّا الْمُحْدِثُ لِذَلِكَ مِنْ أَهْلِ الذِّمَّةِ فَإِنَّهُ فِي أَحَدِ قَوْلَيْ الْعُلَمَاءِ يُنْتَقَضُ عَهْدُهُ وَيُبَاحُ دَمُهُ وَمَالُهُ؛ لِأَنَّهُ خَالَفَ الشُّرُوطَ الَّتِي شَرَطَهَا عَلَيْهِمْ الْمُسْلِمُونَ وَشَرَطُوا عَلَيْهِمْ أَنَّ مَنْ نَقَضَهَا فَقَدْ حَلَّ لَهُمْ مِنْهَا مَا يُبَاحُ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْحَرْبِ. وَاَللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ.
translated_text:
He was asked:

About a Christian priest beside whose house there was a plot containing a ruined, roofless church. None of the Muslims knew when it had fallen into ruin. The priest purchased the plot and built on it, incorporating the church into the construction, repairing its walls, and restoring it. He then began gathering Christians there, and they publicly displayed their religious observances. Some of the authorities summoned him, but he sought strength and support from some Bedouins and openly engaged in wrongdoing.

He answered:

He has no right to establish the church described, even if the remains of an old church stood there in the territory of Syria. The Muslims conquered the territory of Syria by force and took possession of those churches. The scholars agree that they were permitted to demolish them; they disagreed only over whether demolishing them was obligatory.

No one may assist him in establishing this, and anyone who assists him must be punished. As for the non-Muslim under Muslim protection who establishes it, according to one of the two scholarly opinions, his covenant of protection is annulled, and his life may lawfully be taken and his property seized. This is because he has violated the conditions that the Muslims imposed upon them. They also stipulated that anyone who breached those conditions would become subject to whatever is permissible in the case of those at war with the Muslims.

Allah knows best.

translated_text:
He—may Allah have mercy on him—also said:

Concerning the words of Allah Most High:

“O you who believe, fulfil your covenants.”

It has been said that these refer to what Allah and His Messenger have commanded. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, placed this verse at the beginning of the letter he wrote to Amr ibn Hazm when he appointed him governor of Najrān. The letter to Amr contains prescribed obligations, blood-money payments, and practices made obligatory by revealed law.

Allah also says to the believers:

“Remember Allah’s favour upon you and His covenant by which He bound you when you said, ‘We hear and obey.’”

The Quran commentators have mentioned that this verse was revealed concerning the Prophet’s taking the pledge of allegiance from the Ansār on the night of al-Aqabah. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, had bound them by a covenant to what was already obligatory by Allah’s command: to listen to him and obey. Allah reminded them of that covenant so that they would fulfil it, although it imposed nothing beyond what Allah’s command had already made obligatory.

In this verse, He commanded them to remember His favour upon them and His covenant. Thus, He mentioned both grounds of obligation, for the obligation established by revealed law is also binding by virtue of His lordship—that is, His bestowal of blessings upon them. Hence the hadith states:

“Love Allah for the blessings with which He sustains you.”

For this reason, authors writing on the fundamentals of religion customarily begin by discussing the first blessing Allah bestowed upon His servants and the first duty incumbent upon them, and they discuss

“the question of the obligation to thank the Benefactor”: whether this is obligatory by reason as well as by revealed law. This is why the Quran’s approach is to remind people of Allah’s blessings upon them, for these call for gratitude to Him, which consists in fulfilling the obligations prescribed by revealed law.

And His words:

“Allah certainly took a covenant from the Children of Israel, and We appointed twelve leaders from among them. Allah said, ‘I am with you. If you establish prayer, give zakah, believe in My messengers and support them, and lend Allah a good loan…’”

The passage continues up to His words:

“So, for their breaking their covenant, We cursed them and hardened their hearts.”

This covenant concerned what was already obligatory upon them: establishing prayer, giving zakah, believing in the messengers, and supporting them. He stated that He cursed them and hardened their hearts because they broke their covenant, not merely because they disobeyed the command. This indicates that the punishment for violating these obligations, reinforced by covenants, is aggravated by the breach of covenant.

And His words:

“And from those who say, ‘We are Christians,’ We took their covenant, but they neglected a portion of what they had been reminded of.”

The same applies to them. And Allah Most High says:

“Among them are those who made a covenant with Allah: ‘If He gives us of His bounty, we will certainly give charity and be among the righteous.’”

“But when He gave them of His bounty, they withheld it greedily and turned away in aversion.”

“So He caused hypocrisy to take root in their hearts until the Day they meet Him, because they broke their promise to Allah and because they used to lie.”

This explicitly establishes that a vow makes binding what was already obligatory under revealed law. If a person neglects it, he is punished for breaking his promise—that is, his vow. A vow is a solemn promise, as reported concerning Arab usage, and this verse calls a vow a promise.

And His words:

“I will not send him with you until you give me a solemn pledge before Allah that you will bring him back to me, unless you are overwhelmed.” When they gave him their solemn pledge, he said, “Allah is Witness over what we say.”

Returning him to his father was already obligatory upon them, even without a solemn pledge.

Permissible warfare includes defending legally protected lives, property, and sexual inviolability against an aggressor. The concession was granted specifically in peacemaking and warfare because these two situations rest upon bringing hearts together or setting them against one another. When hearts come together, there is peace; when they turn against one another, there is war. Such attraction and aversion can arise from imagined impressions just as they can from realities. Hence poetry can effectively draw people closer or drive them away, powerfully stirring desire and aversion within them, even when its words do not correspond to reality, but work through imagery or figurative comparison.

Since, in lawful peacemaking and warfare, imagining something unreal can serve the same purpose as imagining something real, and equivocal expressions do no more than suggest something unreal while the speaker intends only what is true, such speech is true and truthful from the speaker’s standpoint, while giving the listener an impression that draws him closer in a manner loved by Allah and His Messenger, or drives him away in a manner loved by Allah and His Messenger. He also said—may Allah sanctify his soul:

Chapter

Concerning the conditions that ʿUmar ibn al-Khattāb—may Allah be pleased with him—imposed upon non-Muslims under Muslim protection when he came to Syria. He agreed upon these conditions with them in the presence of the Emigrants and the Helpers—may Allah be pleased with them. The leading scholars of the Muslims follow these conditions in practice, in accordance with the saying of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him:

“Adhere to my sunnah and the sunnah of the rightly guided caliphs after me. Cling to it and hold fast to it with your molar teeth. Beware of newly introduced matters, for every newly introduced matter is an innovation, and every innovation is misguidance.”

And his saying, peace and blessings be upon him:

“Follow the two who come after me: Abū Bakr and ʿUmar.”

For this became a matter of consensus among the Companions of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, who do not agree upon misguidance, based on what they transmitted and understood from the Book of Allah and the sunnah of His Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him.

Sufyān al-Thawrī, from Masrūq ibn ‘Abd al-Rahmān ibn ‘Utbah, who said:

When ‘Umar—may Allah be pleased with him—concluded a peace agreement with the Christians of Syria, he drew up a document stipulating the following conditions:

They must not build any monastery, hermitage, church, or monk’s cell in their towns or the surrounding areas, nor rebuild any that had fallen into ruin. They must not prevent any Muslim from lodging in their churches for three nights, during which they must provide them with food. They must not shelter a spy, conceal treachery against the Muslims, teach their children the Quran, publicly display polytheism, or prevent their relatives from embracing Islam if they wish to do so.

They must show respect to Muslims and rise from their seats for them when they wish to sit down. They must not imitate Muslims in any aspect of their dress—caps, turbans, or sandals—or in the parting of their hair. They must not adopt Muslims’ names of the form “father of,” ride in saddles, wear swords, possess any of the Muslims’ weapons, engrave their rings in Arabic, or sell wine.

They must clip the hair at the front of their heads, retain their distinctive dress wherever they may be, and fasten girdles around their waists. They must not display a cross or any of their scriptures anywhere along the Muslims’ roads, nor bury their dead near Muslims. They must strike their church bells only softly and must not raise their voices when reading in their churches in the presence of Muslims. They must not go out in Palm Sunday processions, raise their voices when accompanying their dead, or display fires in their funeral processions. They must not purchase slaves who have been allotted to Muslims as their shares.

If they violate any of the conditions imposed upon them, they shall have no covenant of protection, and it becomes lawful for the Muslims to subject them to

As for the saying that some ordinary people attribute to the Prophet—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—

“Whoever harms a non-Muslim under Muslim protection has harmed me,”

this is a lie attributed to the Messenger of Allah—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—which no scholar has transmitted. How could it be otherwise, when harming them may be justified or unjustified? Indeed, Allah Most High says:

“And those who harm believing men and believing women for no wrong they have committed have certainly burdened themselves with slander and manifest sin.”

How, then, could he prohibit harming disbelievers unconditionally? And what sin is greater than disbelief? However, in Sunan Abī Dāwūd, al-‘Irbād ibn Sāriyah—may Allah be pleased with him—reports that the Prophet—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—said:

“Allah has not permitted you to enter the homes of the People of the Book without permission, to beat them, or to eat their fruit, provided they have given you what they owe.”

‘Umar ibn al-Khattāb—may Allah be pleased with him—used to say: “Humiliate them, but do not wrong them.”

Safwān ibn Sulaym reports from several sons of the Prophet’s Companions, who related from their fathers that the Messenger of Allah—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—said:

“Beware! Whoever wrongs a person protected by a treaty, deprives him of his due, burdens him beyond his capacity, or takes anything from him without his willing consent—I shall be his adversary on the Day of Resurrection.”

the Messenger of Allah—may Allah bless him and grant him peace:

“No Muslim is liable for jizyah, nor may two qiblahs (directions of prayer) coexist in one land.”

These conditions have been recorded and endorsed in their books by leading scholars of the established schools of law and others. They state that the ruler must require non-Muslims under Muslim protection to distinguish themselves from Muslims in their clothing, hairstyles, honorific bynames, and manner of riding. They must wear garments unlike those worn by Muslims, in colours such as honey, blue, yellow, and dark grey; attach strips of cloth to their caps and turbans; and fasten girdles over their clothes.

Some scholars have stated without qualification that they must both wear distinctive clothing and fasten girdles, while others have said that this is obligatory if stipulated for them. It has already been mentioned that ‘Umar ibn al-Khattāb—may Allah be pleased with him—stipulated all these requirements for them, saying:

“They must not resemble Muslims in any of their clothing, whether caps or anything else, including turbans and sandals.”

Further on, he said:

“He must enforce this upon them wherever they may be, and they must fasten girdles around their waists.”

Those Muslim rulers whom Allah Most High has granted success have continually renewed these conditions upon them. Thus ‘Umar ibn ‘Abd al-‘Azīz—may Allah have mercy on him—renewed them during his caliphate and diligently followed the Sunnah of ‘Umar ibn al-Khattāb—may Allah be pleased with him—

for his knowledge, justice, and adherence to the Quran and Sunnah placed him in a position by which Allah Most High distinguished him above other rulers. Hārūn al-Rashīd, Ja‘far al-Mutawakkil, and others also renewed these conditions. They ordered the demolition of churches that ought to be demolished, such as all the churches in Egypt, concerning which there are two opinions as to whether their demolition is obligatory.

There is no disagreement that churches in territory conquered by force may be demolished upon its conquest. Even if they were left in their inhabitants’ possession because they were the native population—as the Muslims left them in possession of churches in Syria and Egypt—if the outward symbols of Islam subsequently became established in those places, with mosques being built there, then the symbols of unbelief must not coexist with the symbols of Islam. As the Prophet—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—said:

“Two qiblahs may not coexist in one land.”

For this reason, ‘Umar and the Muslims—may Allah be pleased with them—stipulated that they must not publicly display the symbols of their religion.

Furthermore, there is no disagreement among Muslims that Muslim lands may not be dedicated as endowments for monasteries and hermitages, nor are endowments for them valid. Indeed, even if a non-Muslim under Muslim protection were to endow such land and submit the matter to our adjudication, we would not rule the endowment valid. What, then, of dedicating Muslims’ wealth to the unbelievers’ places of worship, where partners are associated with the Most Merciful and Allah and His Messenger are subjected to the vilest abuse?

Among the reasons for the establishment of these churches and the endowments supporting them were

translated_text:
two things.

“The first”: Banū ‘Ubayd al-Qaddāh—whose outward profession was Rāfidism and whose inner reality was hypocrisy—would appoint a Jew as vizier at one time and a Christian at another. That Christian brought in a great many people and built many churches.

You know that, praise be to Allah, we enjoy tremendous blessings, immense favors, abundant bounties, and gifts heaped one upon another—things that most people had never conceived of or imagined. All praise is due to Allah—abundant, pure, and blessed praise, as our Lord loves and is pleased with.

Further on, he said:

Truth continues to triumph, rise, and grow, while falsehood declines, sinks, and dwindles away. Allah has brought the adversaries into submission and utterly humbled them. We, praise be to Allah, have stipulated conditions for this that uphold the honor of Islam and the Sunnah and suppress falsehood and innovation. They have agreed to all of them, but we have held back until they put them into practice. Thus we have not trusted their word

Allah has provided means of honoring Islam and the Sunnah and suppressing unbelief and religious innovation through developments too lengthy to describe in a letter. Likewise, events have unfolded that have brought honor to Islam and subdued the Jews and Christians, after they had become overbearing and acquired power, and had received support from those who supported them in a course of action involving great humiliation for people. This brought honor to the Muslims, united their hearts, and led them to stand up against the Jews and Christians, while bringing humiliation upon the polytheists and the People of the Book. These are among Allah’s greatest blessings upon His believing servants. Describing this would take too long.

I have sent you a letter requesting the work I wrote concerning churches. It consists of several quires in my handwriting, in half-baladī format. Please send it, Allah Most High willing, and seek the assistance of Shaykh Jamāl al-Dīn al-Mizzī, for he can look through the books and locate what is wanted. Also send Judge Abū Ya‘lā’s commentary in the handwriting of Judge Abū al-Husayn—all eleven volumes, if possible; otherwise, one, two, or three volumes from the beginning. He also mentioned other books that he requested from them.

translated_text:
What do the esteemed scholars say (*) concerning a group of non-Muslims under Muslim protection who have been required to wear clothing other than their customary dress and adopt an appearance different from their usual one? The sultan has required them to change their turbans so that they differ from those worn by Muslims. This has caused them great harm on the roads and in the open country, emboldening fools and the rabble against them, who have subjected them to severe abuse. It has encouraged people to humiliate and assault them. May the ruler therefore allow them to return to their former dress and restore their previous situation, provided that they remain distinguishable by an identifying mark? Would this contravene Islamic law or not?

Ibn al-Qayyim said:

Someone deprived of divine guidance and turned away from the path answered them that this was permissible and that the ruler could restore their previous situation.

Our shaykh said:

“The request for a ruling then reached me. I said, ‘They may not be allowed to return to their former dress. They must be kept in the attire that distinguishes them from Muslims.’

“They went away, revised the request, and brought it back in a different form. I said, ‘They may not be allowed to return to their former dress.’

“They went away and brought it back in yet another form. I said, ‘It is the very same question, even if presented in several different forms.’”

Ibn al-Qayyim said:

Then Shaykh al-Islām went to the sultan and addressed him in words that astonished those present. They unanimously agreed to keep them in that attire. All praise belongs to Allah, and all favor comes from Him.
translated_footnote:
(*) Shaykh Nāsir ibn Hamad al-Fahd stated (p. 219):
This passage is quoted from Iʿlām al-Muwaqqiʿīn, 4:193, with minor differences. Its wording in Iʿlām is:

“I shall give you an example that occurred in our time. The sultan ordered that the non-Muslims under Muslim protection be required to change their turbans, making their colors different from those of Muslims’ turbans. This caused an uproar among them and greatly distressed them. It brought benefits, honored Islam, and humbled the disbelievers, much to the Muslims’ delight. Satan then prompted his allies and brethren to frame a request for a ruling through which they could remove this dust (1), as follows:

‘What do the esteemed scholars say concerning a group of non-Muslims under Muslim protection who have been required to wear clothing other than their customary dress and adopt attire different from their usual attire? [The sultan has required them to change their turbans so that they differ from Muslims’ turbans.] (2) This has consequently caused them (3) great harm on the roads and in the open country. It has emboldened fools and shepherds (4) against them, who have subjected them to severe abuse, thereby encouraging (5) their humiliation and assault. May the ruler allow them to return to their former dress and restore their previous situation, provided that they remain distinguishable (6) by an identifying mark? Would this involve (7) a violation of Islamic law or not?’

Someone deprived of divine guidance and turned away from the path answered that this was permissible and that the ruler could restore their previous situation. Our shaykh said: ‘The request for a ruling reached me, and I said, “They may not be allowed to return to their former dress; they must be kept in attire that distinguishes them from Muslims.” They went away, revised the request for a ruling (8), and brought it back in a different form. I said, “They may not be allowed to return to their former dress.” They went away and brought it back in yet another form. I said, “It is the very same question, even if presented in several different forms.”’ Then he went to the sultan (9) and addressed him in words that astonished those present. They unanimously agreed to keep them in that attire. All praise belongs to Allah, and all favor comes from Him.”

(1) This is the reading in Iʿlām: al-ghubār (“dust”). The correct reading is al-ghiyār (“distinctive dress”).
(2) The passage in square brackets is absent from Iʿlām.
(3) Al-Fatāwā: “This consequently caused…” [without “them”].
(4) Al-Fatāwā: “the rabble.”

Concerning monks who share in most of the worldly pursuits of other people: they engage in trade, acquire farms and dovecotes, and undertake other activities commonly pursued by people today. Their monasticism consists merely in their clothing, abstaining from marriage and meat, devotional practices involving impurity, and similar observances. Christians who wish to avoid paying the jizya (poll tax) have now begun adopting this form of monasticism to secure exemption from it. They also receive funds from endowments and votive offerings. Is it permissible to collect the jizya from these people or not? Is it permissible to allow them to reside in Muslim lands while exempting them from the jizya or not? He replied—may Allah be pleased with him:

All praise belongs to Allah.

‘Fight the leaders of disbelief, for they have no regard for their oaths, so that they may desist.’”

He forbade killing the former only because they are people who have withdrawn from others and confined themselves to hermitages. Each is called a recluse. They give their coreligionists no assistance whatsoever in anything harmful to Muslims, nor do they mingle with them in their worldly affairs. Rather, each contents himself with enough to subsist on. Scholars therefore disagreed over killing them, just as they disagreed over killing those who do not harm Muslims by deed or word, such as the blind, the chronically disabled, the elderly, and others like them, as well as women and children.

The majority say that only those who assist them in fighting in some way may be killed; otherwise, they are treated like women and children.

Some, however, say that disbelief alone makes killing lawful, and that women and children were excepted only because they are property. The collection of the jizya is likewise determined on this basis.

As for a monk who assists his coreligionists by deed or word—for example, by offering counsel to which they turn in matters of warfare, or by providing some form of encouragement to fight—scholars agree that he is to be killed if he is overpowered, and that the jizya is collected from him, even if he is a recluse living alone in his place of worship. How much more, then, does this apply to those who are like other Christians in their livelihoods, their mingling with people, and their acquisition of wealth through trade, agriculture, and crafts,

and their establishment of monasteries where others congregate? They are distinguished from others only by things that intensify their disbelief and make them leaders in disbelief, such as acts of worship involving impurities, abstention from marriage and meat, and clothing that is a distinctive mark of disbelief. This is especially so because they sustain the Christian religion through the deceptive tricks they display—about which learned men have written works—their corrupt acts of worship, and their acceptance of their coreligionists’ votive offerings and endowments.

Among them, the sole condition for being a monk is abstention from marriage. Nevertheless, they allow him to be a batrak, a batraq, a priest, or another leader of disbelief whose commands and prohibitions they follow. They may also acquire wealth just as others do. Scholars therefore do not dispute that these are among the Christians most liable to be killed in wartime and to have the jizya collected from them in peacetime. Nor do they dispute that they belong to the same category as those leaders of disbelief about whom al-Siddīq, may Allah be pleased with him, made his statement and recited the words of the Most High:

“Fight the leaders of disbelief.”

This is further clarified by the words of Allah, Glorified and Exalted:

“Indeed, many of the rabbis and monks devour people’s wealth unjustly and turn others away from the way of Allah.”

The Most High also says:

“They have taken their rabbis and monks, as well as the Messiah, son of Mary, as lords besides Allah, though they were commanded only to worship one God. There is no deity except Him. Exalted is He above whatever they associate with Him.”

No one who understands what he is saying would say this. The confusion arose only because the word “monk” is ambiguous and has several meanings. We have explained that the transmitted report is qualified and restricted in scope, and that it clarifies the report traced back to the Prophet on this matter. The scholars agree that the reason for the prohibition is what we have explained.

The jizya is therefore collected from those described here, without any doubt or disagreement among the leading scholars. It is to be taken from them, and no Muslim land conquered by force and subjected to the jizya may lawfully be left in their possession. Accordingly, scholars of the established schools—the Hanafīs, Mālikīs, Shāfiʿīs, and Hanbalīs—have not disputed that Egypt’s land was subject to kharāj (land tax). This is established by the authentic hadith in Sahīh Muslim, in which the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Iraq will withhold its dirhams and qafīz measures, Syria will withhold its mudd measures and dinars, and Egypt will withhold its irdabb measures and dirhams, and you will return to where you began.”

However, when the Muslims grew in number, they changed the assessment of the lands of al-Sawād, in the early Abbasid period, from a fixed land tax to a share of the produce. Likewise, they changed the arrangement in Egypt until they themselves received its revenues, as is the case today; hence the land tax was lifted from it. Consequently, these unbelievers’ places of worship have endowments the like of which are not found for the Muslims’ mosques and residences devoted to learning and worship, even though the land was subject to kharāj by the agreement of the Muslim scholars. No one who believes in Allah and His Messenger would do such a thing. Rather, it is done only by unbelievers, hypocrites, and those Muslim rulers whom they have misled about this matter. Once the Muslim rulers understand the situation, they will act in this matter as Allah and His Messenger have commanded. Allah, glorified and exalted is He, knows best. May Allah bless Muhammad.
